title: Rav Huna the Exilarch
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Rabbi’s time. In [Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kilayim.9.3.8), Rabbi said: “If Rav Huna the Exilarch came up here, I would seat him above me, for he is from Judah and I am from Benjamin; he is from the male line and I am from the female line.” Once Rabbi Chiyya Rabbah came in to him and said to him, “Rav Huna is outside.” Rabbi’s face turned pale. He said to him, “His coffin has come.” In [Horayot 11b](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.11b.2) Rabbi asked Rabbi Chiyya: “Someone like me — what is the law concerning [the ruler’s sin-offering] goat?” He said to him: “Your rival is in Babylonia”; Hyman considers the reference undoubtedly to Rav Huna the Exilarch.[^1]

In [Ruth Rabbah, beginning of chapter 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Ruth_Rabbah.3.1): “Rav Huna the Exilarch asked Rav Chisda: What is the meaning of ‘Remove the turban’?” etc. Hyman considers this a scribal error and proposes reading as in [Gittin 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.7a.13-15): “The Exilarch asked Rav Huna; meanwhile Rav Huna rose to relieve himself; Rav Chisda said to him.” In [Jerusalem Talmud Sotah, chapter 9, end of halakhah 15](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.9.15.7): “The Exilarch sent and asked Rav Chisdai — Rabbi Yochanan heard.” Hyman argues that Ruth Rabbah’s reading arose through erroneous copying from these two places.[^2]

notes.text: Horayot leaves the rival in Babylonia unnamed. [Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=957&lang=en) likewise identifies him as Rav Huna and explicitly observes that the name is absent from the Gemara.

Ruth Rabbah has Rav Huna the Exilarch asking Rabbi Chisdai. In Gittin the Exilarch asks Rav Huna, and Rav Chisda answers when Rav Huna steps away. In the Yerushalmi the Exilarch sends a question to Rav Chisdai. Hyman proposes that the midrash conflated the two accounts.
